findings.title: Spawn or entry into the stadium pocket (nav component 16): no way out, dies to the zone
findings.where: zoneGoal() lines 121-141 (goal must be in our own component), zoneLegs() 172-176, zoneCheck() 144-170; brain.js legs(); no caller of nav.hopPlan anywhere in bot/lib
findings.evidence: nav.js builds a second walking component of 10033 cells (40,000 m2, bbox x -375..-179, y -2..256, the stadium) that only nav.hopPlan() joins to the main one; `grep hopPlan bot/lib/{brain,mover,tactics,economy,stance,senses,firecontrol}.js` finds nothing. Official replay (replay/mech16.jsonl.gz): mech 2 spawns at (-307.02, 106.14, z -9.23) = component 16, stays grounded inside it for 129 s with no walking transition out and is last seen at t=209.6 with hp 3 (1 of 16 spawns). Dev-simulator test /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-yang-mills-workbench/c2b3cfae-3f5d-5b6f-8fe6-a6e757d1bb60/scratchpad/mechbot/tools/review_safety/t_bowl.js (our mech moved into component 16 before the first tick, 16 seeds): in 7 seeds (2,4,8,9,11,13,15) it never leaves and dies with cause 'zone' (456-1399 zone damage, 65-402 decisions in ZONE/zone legs, peak height above ground 4-31 m); the other runs got out only through the accidental air jet of the next finding (peaks 25-96 m) or the match ended first. Mechanism: findPath to a goal in another component returns ok:false with a partial path ending at the wall, the stuck ladder jets for 1 s only, and continuous ground boost outside the zone keeps energy near 0. t_hopplan.js: nav.hopPlan returns a plan from 272/272 sampled cells of the component (climb 1.5-9.7 m, median 6.6 m, call <= 5.3 ms). Protocol section 7: "Anything taller is a wall unless your feet are already above it: jump and jet (boost in the air) until they clear the edge, then move over it."
findings.fix: Use nav.hopPlan when nav.component(me) is not nav.mainComponent and the goal is in another component: walk to plan.launch without spending energy, wait until energy covers the hop, jump, hold boost until feet >= plan.apexZ, then steer to plan.land; add plan.walkLen + hopLen + the wait to the zone margin so ZONE starts early enough. A working prototype is in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-yang-mills-workbench/c2b3cfae-3f5d-5b6f-8fe6-a6e757d1bb60/scratchpad/mechbot/tools/review_safety/lib_fix.patch (mover.pocketExit, zoneCheck length, brain legs hook; a patched COPY of bot/lib is in tools/review_safety/lib_fix): with it the 7 failing seeds give 0 zone deaths (zone damage 0, one seed 107), zone walks in the main component stay 60/60, fuzz and edge cases stay clean. Run: MECH_LIB=tools/review_safety/lib_fix ./bun tools/review_safety/t_bowl.js 2,4,8,9,11,13,15.

findings.title: selectTarget() throws TypeError (null best) when a wounded attacker hides while an unseen drone or mech keeps hitting us
findings.where: selectTarget(): line 104 `let best = null, bestI = -1`, line 109 `(A - tr.a + 1)`, line 125 `best.losOut`
findings.evidence: `V = 1 + Math.min(2, (me.hp / A) * tr.a / ((A - tr.a + 1) * tauMed))`: A only sums tracks with a recent line of fire, but tr.a of a candidate without one is still dmg3/3 while it has >= 3 damage samples, so the denominator goes negative, the index drops below the start value bestI = -1, `best` stays null and line 125 dereferences it. Logged: "brain stage assess failed at tick 27: TypeError: null is not an object (evaluating 'best.losOut') at selectTarget (tactics.js:125:57)". Reproduction with legal observations, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-yang-mills-workbench/c2b3cfae-3f5d-5b6f-8fe6-a6e757d1bb60/scratchpad/mechbot/tools/review_safety/t_select_null2.js: mech (hp 400, 50-80 m) fires a 3-round burst, steps behind a building but stays listed (protocol section 8: "you keep tracking its real, current position for `memory_s` (5 s) after it leaves view"), a drone we never saw hits once per second: the assess stage throws in 30/30 random street scenes for 11 consecutive decisions, and in 30/30 without a map. t_select_null.js: also at target hp 100 and 40, not at 1400. The stage wrapper catches it, so no protocol error: the previous target is kept, killSecure and the per-track index stay stale, counters.errors rises. When there is no current target the same state silently selects nobody. Random fuzz (175k combat-shaped decisions) does not reach this state; it needs this sequence.
findings.fix: Line 109: divide by `Math.max(1, A - tr.a + 1)`; line 104: `bestI = -Infinity`; line 125: `!!best && best.losOut`. Checked on the patched copy (MECH_LIB=tools/review_safety/lib_fix): 0/30 scenes throw with and without a map; fuzz, edge cases and zone walks unchanged.

findings.title: boost is commanded while airborne: in the air boost is the jet, so one airborne tick outside the zone turns into a 40 m climb that empties the tank
findings.where: legs() lines 301-319 (no grounded check before the final boost rules); sources: mover.js zoneLegs() line 175, shellDodge() line 215, brain.js retreatLegs() lines 211 and 230, fightLegs() 268/289/290
findings.evidence: Protocol section 6, `boost`: "On the ground while moving: run at `boost_speed`, draining `boost_drain`/s energy. In the air: jet upward (`jet_accel`, capped at `max_rise_speed`), draining `jet_drain`/s." No leg routine looks at self.grounded when it asks for a running boost. /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-yang-mills-workbench/c2b3cfae-3f5d-5b6f-8fe6-a6e757d1bb60/scratchpad/mechbot/tools/review_safety/t_airborne_boost.js (ZONE mode outside the circle, vertical motion integrated from the protocol numbers jump_speed 11, jet_accel 34, gravity 22, max_rise_speed 10, jet_drain 15): after a single 1.5 m ledge drop the brain holds boost on 46 consecutive airborne decisions, peaks 41.6 m above ground, lands 6.8 s later with no energy and covers 211 m in 16 s instead of 244 m; with boost suppressed in the air: 4 airborne decisions, 1.6 m, 243 m. Seen in closed loop too: sim_probe.js flags `boost:true` with self.grounded false in FIGHT/dodge, and the pocket runs above show climbs of 25-96 m. The feedback is self-sustaining because jetting keeps the mech airborne and ZONE keeps boost on while in_zone is false.
findings.fix: In legs(), before `mover.stuckCheck()`: `if (cmd.boost && !B.me.grounded && !B.wantJet) cmd.boost = false` (stuckCheck runs after it and still sets the deliberate phase-2 jet; B.wantJet is the flag of the pocket hop). Checked on the patched copy: boost held on 1 airborne decision, peak 1.6 m. Apply together with the pocket-exit fix, because today's accidental jets are the only way the bot leaves component 16.

findings.title: Wall-clock gates decide what is computed, so the same observations give different actions when a decision is stalled
findings.where: brain.js evalMaybe() line 162, act() lines 361 and 369-373 (slowMs -> budgetScale 0.5 for 20 decisions); mover.js lines 52 and 154 (planMinMs); stance.js line 223
findings.evidence: Unloaded, the bot is deterministic: identical action files for the recorded simulator match (2929 decisions) on Bun twice and on Node 22, and for the worst-case stream (6000 decisions) twice. With three busy loops pinned to the bot's CPU (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-yang-mills-workbench/c2b3cfae-3f5d-5b6f-8fe6-a6e757d1bb60/scratchpad/mechbot/tools/review_safety/busy.js + run_heavy.js) one of two runs diverged from the reference: 210 of 3000 action lines differ, first at line 55. t_gates.js feeds byte-identical observations in-process and only changes the gate outcome: planMinMs gate closed -> 878 of 3000 decisions differ, first at #54 (the same decision as in the loaded run); slowMs = 0 -> 48 differ; optional stages skipped -> 43 differ. Protocol section 6: "`seed` is yours: seed your RNG with it to make your bot reproducible." The real sandbox has its own CPU, so this mostly makes practice and simulator results depend on host load (the machine ran at load average 15-20 during this review).
findings.fix: Make the budgets work-based and fixed (ray counts, A* expansions): the measured worst stage costs sum to 5.8 ms (stage_cost.js: findPath 2.3 ms, posEval 0.83, hide slice 0.35), so no gate is needed below about 30 ms. Keep the clock only as an emergency brake (skip optional stages when more than ~35 ms of the 50 are gone) and drop slowMs/budgetScale, or make budgetScale depend on a work counter.

findings.title: Outside the zone the ground boost is pulsed at 15% duty once the tank is empty (boost whenever energy > 1)
findings.where: zoneLegs() line 175 `cmd.boost = me.energy > 1`; brain.js legs() line 317 `if (cmd.boost && B.me.energy < 2) cmd.boost = false`
findings.evidence: Protocol section 7: "Energy regenerates at `energy_regen`/s after `energy_regen_delay` s without spending." Spending every 1.8 energy the moment it arrives pays the 0.6 s delay on every cycle. /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-yang-mills-workbench/c2b3cfae-3f5d-5b6f-8fe6-a6e757d1bb60/scratchpad/mechbot/tools/review_safety/t_boost_pulse.js (energy model from boost_drain 17, energy_regen 18, energy_regen_delay 0.6; 90 s walk toward a far circle): brain as is boosts on 15% of decisions after the first 30 s, mean 12.9 m/s, 1197 m; a refill-to-60-then-spend rule boosts 47%, 15.4 m/s, 1401 m (+17%). The same pulsing keeps energy near 0, which also disables the stuck jet (needs energy > 5) and lightning (lightReserve 35). Depends on the stated regen rule, which no recorded stream here verifies.
findings.fix: Hysteresis: after the tank drops below 2, do not boost again until energy >= about 50-60 (or the zone margin is negative and the remaining distance is short); keep the reserve the pocket hop needs.

findings.title: nav.setBody runs inside senseSelf on every cube pickup: the largest single cost of a match, never warmed up
findings.where: senseSelf() lines 94-98; warmUp() in brain.js lines 66-98 always sends cubes 0
findings.evidence: Real bot process pinned with taskset -c 0, CPU time from /proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/schedstat (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-yang-mills-workbench/c2b3cfae-3f5d-5b6f-8fe6-a6e757d1bb60/scratchpad/mechbot/tools/review_safety/cube_spike.js, 6 fresh processes): main thread 3.3-6.3 ms on the first resize, 3.7-9.4 ms on the second, 1.3-2.0 ms from the sixth on; summed over all 7 threads (JIT compile) up to 23.6 ms. Every other decision of those runs: p50 0.22, p99 0.69, max 3.7 ms. nav.js documents "about 2 ms". Kill drops arrive in bursts, so 3-4 such decisions follow each other. Still inside the 50 ms budget and inside the spec's max <= 25 ms in CPU terms; it also trips slowMs (15 ms) under any stall and so feeds the previous finding. For scale, the rest is cheap: worst-case stream (15 mechs + 3 drones, 10 projectiles, 22 loot objects, 12 spots including the stadium and the map corners, 6000 decisions, real process): main thread mean 0.39, p99 1.32, max 5.6 ms; all threads p99 3.7, max 13.6 ms; recorded match: main max 7.1 ms.
findings.fix: In createBrain (hello budget, start-up is 0.7-1.1 s of 20 s) call nav.setBody for cubes 1..12 two or three times and restore the base body so the function is compiled before the first pickup; apply a resize only on a decision without a plan, or at most once per second.

findings.title: Own body size is taken from self.stats.radius / height when present; the protocol only promises eye_height and muzzle_height there
findings.where: senseSelf() lines 77-81 (`me.radius = cnum(st.radius, m.radius * scale, 0.5, 30)`, same for height)
findings.evidence: Protocol section 10: "radius, height, eye, and muzzle height all scale by 1 + 0.05 x cubes (`self.stats` shows your current `eye_height` and `muzzle_height`)". The cube formula is only the fallback when stats.radius is missing. If the server leaves stats.radius at the [mech] base value 2.5 (the kit stream only has cubes = 0, so nothing here shows which), the navigation body stays 2.5 m while the real cylinder is 3.75 m at 10 cubes, against a nav wall margin of 0.3 m. Argued from the text, not observed. edge_cases.js case 'cubes 40, stats not scaled' runs without error either way.
findings.fix: `me.radius = Math.max(cnum(st.radius, 0, 0.5, 30), m.radius * scale)` and the same for height; keep eye_height and muzzle_height from stats as now.

summary:
Scope: crashes, protocol errors, performance of the brain (bot/lib/brain.js, senses.js, tactics.js, mover.js, firecontrol.js, economy.js, stance.js, params.js) plus bot.js, aim.js, world.js, nav.js read as dependencies. Nothing under bot/ was edited (md5 of all files unchanged). My scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-yang-mills-workbench/c2b3cfae-3f5d-5b6f-8fe6-a6e757d1bb60/scratchpad/mechbot/tools/review_safety/ ; library notes were written to /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-yang-mills-workbench/c2b3cfae-3f5d-5b6f-8fe6-a6e757d1bb60/scratchpad/mechbot/notes/lib_bug_reports.md.

Result in one line: no protocol error and no uncaught crash was found; one internal exception (selectTarget) is real and reproducible, and the two findings that cost score are behavioural: no exit from the stadium pocket, and boost sent while airborne.

Nine findings, ordered by cost to the score:
1. Stadium pocket (nav component 16): the brain never calls nav.hopPlan. 7 of 16 dev-simulator runs started there die to the zone; the official replay has a mech spawning there and dying there. A prototype fix (tools/review_safety/lib_fix.patch, on a copy of bot/lib) removes all 7 zone deaths.
2. tactics.js selectTarget: TypeError on `best.losOut` in 30/30 scenes of "wounded attacker hides, unseen drone keeps hitting". Caught by the stage wrapper, so the old target is kept. Three-line fix checked on the copy.
3. boost while airborne is the jet: 46 decisions of climbing to 41.6 m after one ledge drop outside the zone. One-line guard checked on the copy.
4. Wall-clock gates: identical observations give different actions when a decision is stalled (210 of 3000 under forced CPU contention; cause isolated to the planMinMs gate).
5. Ground boost outside the zone is pulsed at 15% duty instead of about 47%.
6. nav.setBody on every cube pickup: 3.3-9.4 ms main thread, up to 23.6 ms over all threads; the largest single cost, within budget.
7. Own radius/height trusted from self.stats, which the protocol does not promise (argued from the text, not observed).
8. Off-map track positions cost 6-22 ms per decision (illegal input only).
9. bot.js fallback policy and `end` handling (minor, reported to the library notes).

What checked out clean:
- Protocol usage: fire slots, laser hold/release and the `charge` / `min_charge` / `min_frac` / `hold_s` names, reload, take with drop slot, pick index, absolute [yaw, pitch], world-frame move, zone, drops, offer, events, sounds, beams all match protocol.md and the schema. About 40,000 answers from the real process: 0 invalid, 0 wrong tick, 0 bad lines, 0 missing. In dev-simulator matches 12 of 12 takes succeeded, 37 of 37 offers were answered on the first tick, and 37 of 49 laser releases hit.
- Odd but legal observations (45 cases, with and without map): slot 1 null, both slots non-gun or empty, gun in slot 1, no mechs, 15 mechs + 12 drones, npc only, required-only actor fields, hp 0, cubes 40 and 200, zone radius 0, t beyond 480, first tick, tick gaps of 10 and 100, self outside the map / in a building / on a roof / airborne, world-only and nav-only: 0 throws, 0 stage errors, 0 NaN in the raw action.
- Fuzz: 30,000 legal + 24,000 garbage decisions with map, 36,000 without, 175,000 combat-shaped: 0 throws, 0 stage errors, 0 NaN.
- Conformance: PASS 300/300 on Bun 1.4.4 and on Node 22.
- Start-up on one CPU: ready in 0.69-0.79 s wall (0.66-0.75 s CPU, 7 threads, peak RSS 71-78 MB); 3.7-4.7 s with the CPU shared four ways; limit 20 s. No file writes and no sockets under strace; works with unwritable HOME and TMPDIR.
- Per-decision cost, real process, CPU time from /proc schedstat: worst-case stream (15 mechs + 3 drones, 10 projectiles, expensive spots, 6000 decisions) main thread mean 0.39 ms, p99 1.32, max 5.6; all threads max 13.6 ms. The stage costs in isolation sum to 5.8 ms; findPath with 4000 expansions is at most 2.3 ms.
- Memory: RSS 71-92 MB over 6000 decisions, flat (limit 512 MB). No state grows without bound: tracks capped at 64, loot maps at 128, shells at 12.
- Determinism when not stalled: identical actions on Bun twice and on Node 22 (2929 decisions), and on the worst-case stream twice (6000 decisions).

Caveats:
- The machine ran at load average 15-20 from other jobs for the whole review, so wall-clock latencies here are not usable (up to 190 ms seen with 0.4 ms of CPU). All performance numbers above are CPU time. The 24-47 ms setBody times printed by replay_attr.js, sim_probe.js and bigbody.js are that pollution; cube_spike.js is the authoritative measurement.
- The real sandbox was emulated with taskset -c 0 only; no Docker run and no cgroup CPU quota or 512 MB limit was applied.
- sim/ was being edited by another agent during the review, so simulator outcomes for a given seed changed over the hour. The pocket result (7 of 16) is from the simulator as it stood at about 06:14-06:20 UTC.
- The airborne-boost and boost-pulse numbers come from my own integration of the protocol's movement and energy numbers, not from the server.

Open question, not a finding: in the kit's real stream the gun cooldown reads 0.19 / 0.09 / 0 at successive decisions and shots come every 6 ticks. With readyCd 0.05 the brain can only press at 0, so 0.30 s per shot (55 of 55 in-burst intervals in the recorded simulator match). Whether pressing at 0.09 yields 0.25 s on the real server is not shown by any data here; the forensics note that all 1118 replay fire events fall on odd ticks.

findings.title: Gun trigger is only pulled when the cooldown read-out is <= 0.05 s: one shot per 0.30 s instead of 0.24 s
findings.where: run(), line 154 (gunReady) with PARAMS.readyCd = 0.05 in params.js line 19; lightning on line 234 already uses readyCd + 0.05
findings.evidence: Doctrine D8 asks for the trigger down at cooldown <= 0.1 s. After a shot the read-outs are 0.19, 0.09, 0 (sim/README.md says the recorded real stream shows the same); at 0.09 the brain keeps the trigger up, so the shot that could leave on the second tick of that decision leaves one decision later. tools/review_tactics/s01_cadence.js: 64 shots / 30 s, gap 0.300 s shipped; 72 shots, gap 0.236 s with readyCd 0.10 (95 -> 108 dmg/s on a standing target at 50-100 m). s18_pershot_latency.js (8 seeds x 60 s, walking target): 88-92 -> 104-107 dmg/s at 75 m, 83 -> 99-102 at 110 m. stats4.js over 60 squad matches: 5560 decisions with a loaded gun, listed target, clear line and trigger up only because the read-out was between 0.05 and 0.10 s, against 5963 trigger-down decisions. s16_duel_matrix.js (1 v 1 at 75 m against a standing exact-lead shooter, 24 duels): kills 13/24 shipped, 22/24 with readyCd 0.10. Paired squad A/B in the dev simulator, 150 seeds: +0.23 +- 0.15.
findings.fix: Set readyCd to one decision period (decide_every / tick_hz = 0.10 s, read from hello.config) for the gun and mortar. Then lead for the tick the shot really leaves on: tl = 0.05 when the read-out is <= 0.05, else 0.10, in predictSelf / gunSolve / predYaw (s18: about +1 to +2 points of hit rate at 110 m on top; PARAMS.latency 0.10 for every shot is 0.05 s too long for a ready gun).

findings.title: LAST-STAND is declared in winnable fights (65-70% hp, even 1 v 1) and its bastion legs stand still under fire
findings.where: chooseStance() line 110 (enterLS), fightLegs() lines 250-254 and findBastion() 184-213; tactics.js decideMode() lines 164-166 (doomed); stance.js line 160 (mustDisengage)
findings.evidence: doomed / enterLS = hp < A*(tCover+1) with A the 3 s damage average (inflated by rear hits and by walking straight to cover) or prior dps of every aiming mech. s15_duel_trace.js (-244,14): hit from behind at t=0.6, DISENGAGE, HEAL at 68%, LAST-STAND at t=2.5 with hp 905/1400 against ONE mech (A=165, tCover 4.8 s), walks to a wall cell and stops; the shooter lands 31 of 32 shots and we die in all 3 seeds. s16_duel_matrix.js, 24 duels at 75 m near cover against a standing exact-lead gun: shipped kills 13/24 (enemy in front) and 11/24 (enemy behind), 11-12 deaths, standing still on 30-33% of the decisions with a line on us; with the bastion disabled (override bastionWall -100): 24/24 and 23/24 kills, 0 deaths. s08_doomed.js: three mechs that only aim and never shoot -> LAST-STAND at t=0.2 with 1400 hp. stats2.js, 60 squad matches: 1.35 entries per match, mean hp fraction at entry 0.70, 19% of all decisions in LAST-STAND, 60% of those with speed < 2 m/s. Squad A/B (150 seeds) with the bastion off: +0.12 +- 0.08.
findings.fix: Remove the bastion stop: in LAST-STAND keep the normal stand-off legs with the jink (if a wall cell is wanted, strafe along the wall with reversals, never moveTo and stay). Replace doomed / enterLS / mustDisengage by the D3 table (LOSING only: 1 threat hp < 35% and target >= ours + 0.10; 2 threats < 50%; 3-5 < 60%; 6+), count only mechs that actually damaged us in the last 3 s, and never enter LAST-STAND with fewer than 2 such attackers unless hp < 25% and no hide cell is reachable.

findings.title: Fights are broken off far above the D3 thresholds, and the decision flips with the distance to cover
findings.where: decideMode() lines 141-184 (hE, fightOk line 157, HEAL lines 167-169); stance.js applyStance() line 160 (mustDisengage, no hold time)
findings.evidence: The code still uses the section 4 H_esc inequality (hp - A*(tCover+1) - 150 >= tau*A) that Doctrine D3 replaced. tools/review_tactics/stats5.js, 60 squad matches: 353 FIGHT -> DISENGAGE/HEAL transitions (5.9 per match) at a mean hp fraction of 0.82; only 12 are LOSING by D3; with at most one mech having a line: 171 transitions, 167 at hp >= 35%, 110 at hp >= 70%; 16% of the in-contact decisions that D3 calls not-losing are spent in DISENGAGE or HEAL. Because tCover shrinks as we approach the hide cell, arriving makes fightOk true again: stats2.js counts 4.1 FIGHT -> DISENGAGE -> FIGHT cycles inside 2.5 s per match and only 31% of hide-leg episodes reach their cell. s17_duel_d3.js (same 24 duels as s16, bastion off, readyCd 0.10): mean time to kill 16.6 s -> 12.2 s (enemy in front) and 24.5 s -> 14.5 s (enemy behind) when the inequality is neutralised (hEscBase -5000) and HEAL is limited to < 35% with exit at 70%. Squad A/B on top of findings 1 and 2, 120 seeds: +0.14 +- 0.16. D3 cites -0.41 and -1.1 for early retreats on real scores.
findings.fix: Implement the D3 LOSING predicate literally as the only way from FIGHT to DISENGAGE (plus the finish exception: target < 20% hp and <= 2 threats), with a 5-point hp hysteresis and a 1.5 s minimum stay; drop hE, tau*A and mustDisengage from the SQUAD path. Keep shooting and keep the laser charging while retreating, as D3 says.

findings.title: Jink is switched off for the whole reload against any target that carries a laser or mortar (the practice hunter is gun + laser)
findings.where: fightLegs() lines 280-283 (relocating / doJink)
findings.evidence: relocating = gunBusy && (tgt.hasLaser || tgt.hasMortar) removes the strafe reversals, so we move steadily for about 2.4 s of every 5.3 s gun cycle; D1 says a steadily moving target is hit 84% of the time and one that changed velocity 22%. tools/review_tactics/s09_relocate.js (exact first-order gun shooter at 100 m that never fires its second weapon, 4 seeds x 60 s): hits taken while our gun reloads 1.04 per s with a gun-only enemy, 2.14 per s when it also holds a laser (2.11 mortar); damage taken per minute 2936 -> 4118 (+40%); lateral reversals during reloads 124 -> 22.
findings.fix: Delete the !relocating term from doJink (keep the seeded reversals during the reload). If M3 is wanted, do it only as the existing reloadhide (a hide cell within 8 m), never as a straight run in the open.

findings.title: A second weapon is rarely taken: more than half of the matches end gun-only although a laser or lightning pickup lay within 60 m
findings.where: chooseLoot() lines 48-86 (open requires A = 0, no mech within 150 m, hp >= 90%); tactics.js decideMode() line 170 (FIGHT before LOOT whenever a target is within 150 m or hp < 90%)
findings.evidence: tools/review_tactics/stats3.js, 60 squad matches: 34 end with an empty second slot; in 45 a ground-level laser or lightning pickup was known within 60 m while the slot was empty; in 28 a ground-level laser was known within 60 m for >= 3 s while we held none (mean 16.6 s) and 14 of those never held a laser; only 17 matches ever held one. Value of the weapon, s11_laser.js: gun only 84 dmg/s against a steadily walking target at 100 m, gun + laser 218; 56 -> 189 against a strafing one; beams hit 92-100% at 100-190 m with the 2.40 s cycle (the laser fire control itself is correct). D6 / D7: always want a laser, detour to a laser pickup within 60 m when we have none (35 m for other wanted weapons), in contact too.
findings.fix: Add the D6 power grab as a leg rule that runs in FIGHT, HEAL and DISENGAGE as well: when slot 1 is empty (or holds no laser) and a remembered ground-level laser is within 60 m of path (lightning 35 m), hp > 50% (12 m when LOSING), walk to it with the strafe blended in; hands() already sends take. Remove the hp >= 90% and no-mech-within-150 m conditions for weapon pickups.

findings.title: A drone that touches us takes over the target during a duel: 8/8 won duels become 1/8
findings.where: selectTarget() lines 83-130 (I = V / tau, x0.5 for a drone on line 112, x0.3 without a line on line 111)
findings.evidence: A 350 hp drone has a tau four times shorter than a fresh mech, so 0.5 * V / tau beats the mech as soon as our hp (and with it V of the mech) drops or the mech loses the line for one decision. tools/review_tactics/s20_drone_switch.js, open ground, standing exact-lead gun shooter at 75 m, bastion disabled, 8 seeds: without a drone 8/8 kills, 0 deaths, 14.0 s per kill; with one drone 35 m behind us 1/8 kills, 7 deaths; while the mech lived 45% of the decisions targeted the drone, 78 of 211 trigger decisions went to it, and 43 hits were taken in the back (x1.5) from the mech. stats2.js: 1038 decisions with a drone as target in 60 squad matches (17 per match). Related: in HEAL (hp < 90%, no mech line) holdFire also stops fire at a drone that keeps hitting us, which blocks regeneration until we have walked 90 m away (seen in a match trace with the drone at 140 hp).
findings.fix: Make the order lexicographic: a drone is a candidate only when no mech has had a line on us or damaged us in the last 3 s, or when the drone itself is a kill-secure (<= 3 gun hits) and the current mech target is not. Count drone damage as contact for holdFire (shoot it back, it is 8 shots and 2 cubes), and keep the torso veto on the mech.

findings.title: Path flip-flop on partial paths: 42 s oscillating in place, then 1460 hp of zone damage
findings.where: plan() lines 23-36 and moveTo() lines 46-67 (maxExpand = PARAMS.pathExpand 4000, partial results followed, slide-straight fallback); zoneCheck() lines 154-163 (straight * 1.3 when the plan is not ok); stuckCheck() keys on speed only
findings.evidence: tools/review_tactics/s22_zone_seed.js, dev-simulator squad seed 156: from t=152 to t=194 the mech stays within 3 m of (49,222) with the commanded direction alternating between (-0.65,-0.76) and (+0.66,+0.75), 10-15 reversals per 5 s, stuck counter 0, 6 plans per 2 s, boost burnt from 100 to 0; zoneMargin was shown as 30 s at t=152 although the real path is 439 m (37 s); the zone closes over it at t=192, 25.5 s outside, hp 1512 -> 52. s23_partial_path.js at that spot (goal 57 m away behind a long building): findPath with maxExpand 2000 / 4000 returns partial paths of 0-3 m whose first heading is -142 or +50 degrees depending on a 2 m change of the start; with the nav default 25000 it returns the complete 439 m path after 4800 expansions in 1.2-6.3 ms. The mover alternates between that stub and its no-path fallback (steer straight at the goal into the wall). stats7_noprogress.js: 2 of 60 matches have such windows (8 windows of 5 s); stats6_zone.js: this is the only stretch outside the zone in those 60 matches. nav.findPath behaves as documented (ok / partial), the fault is in the caller.
findings.fix: Plan zone and other must-reach goals with the nav default budget (25000; measured 1-6 ms here), spread over ticks if needed; never follow a partial path whose end is not at least 10 m closer to the goal than we are; keep the last complete path instead of replanning from scratch every 0.5 s; in zoneCheck treat a not-ok plan as unknown length (assume late: go to the next centre now) instead of straight * 1.3; add a progress test to stuckCheck (distance to goal not reduced by 5 m in 3 s while commanded -> abandon / re-goal) and make zoneLegs honour it.

findings.title: The cubes of our own kills are left on the ground in 71% of the kills
findings.where: chooseLoot() lines 54-56 and 70-73 (killDrop needs quiet and A = 0); tactics.js decideMode() line 170; brain.js retreatLegs() lines 203 and 219 (no mech within 150 m, 3 s without a line)
findings.evidence: tools/review_tactics/stats2.js, 60 squad matches (seeds 101-160): 174 kills; within 20 s of a kill the cube count rose by 0.80 on average (a kill drops the victim's cubes plus two) and 123 kills gave nothing. stats3.js: matches end with a mean of 2.55 cubes and 1.22 upgrades; 12602 decisions had a ground cube known within 40 m, 7762 of them not in a loot leg. The conditions are stricter than section 5 ("when no mech has a line of fire") and than D6 ("collect the cubes of our kills at once", cube detour within 70 m at hp > 50%, 40 m lower, 12 m when LOSING).
findings.fix: On a kill event store the drop point and make it a leg goal in every mode: within 70 m at hp > 50%, 40 m below, 12 m when LOSING, zone permitting, with the strafe blended in while a mech has a line; drop the A = 0 / quiet / nobody-within-150 m conditions for kill cubes, and remember cubes for 40 s (D6).

findings.title: HEAL starts at any hp below 90% as soon as nobody has a line for 1 s, and ends only at 90%
findings.where: decideMode() line 169 with PARAMS.healExit 0.9 (also used as the entry level), line 183 holdFire
findings.evidence: D3: HEAL only out of contact below 55%, or below 90% within 6 s of a LOSING retreat; leave at 70%; no hiding at hp >= 55% when not LOSING (measured -0.5 [S]). tools/review_tactics/stats2.js, 60 squad matches: 59% of all HEAL decisions happen at hp >= 55% and 34% at hp >= 70%; HEAL ends at a mean hp fraction of 0.61 because the hunter arrives first. While in HEAL the brain neither loots (lootHpf 0.9) nor pulls. Squad A/B with healExit 0.7 alone, 120 seeds: +0.12 +- 0.09.
findings.fix: Enter HEAL only when (no line on us for 1.5 s and hp < 55%) or (hp < 90% and a LOSING retreat ended less than 6 s ago); leave at 70% (preset healExit) or when a mech gets a line and we are not LOSING. Above 55% and out of contact go for cubes, the laser or the next duel instead.

findings.title: Torso veto runs after the triggers are decided and can park the torso between two enemies, shooting neither
findings.where: aimVeto() lines 299-321, called after fc.run() in brain.js line 366
findings.evidence: tools/review_tactics/s03_aimveto.js: a 120 hp kill-secure mech 70 m east, a shooter 70 m west. The brain keeps the kill-secure target for 87 decisions after t=3 while the commanded yaw sits 94-99 degrees off it (80 degrees from the attacker): 0 trigger decisions on the target in 8.7 s, and the attacker is not aimed at either; 101 vetoes counted. The first vetoed decision still has fire=true computed for the pre-veto aim. In squad matches (stats2.js / stats4.js, 60 matches): 11.8 veto decisions per match, 373 decisions with gun ready, clear line, torso more than 17 degrees off and no shot; 747 ready-gun decisions with the torso more than 20 degrees off the target.
findings.fix: Make it a target rule, not an aim clamp, and run it before fire control: if an attacker of >= 60 dps is more than 80 degrees off the current target, either switch the target to that attacker, or (target is a kill-secure / under 25% hp) keep the target and skip the veto for up to 1.5 s. Never output an aim that points at neither. Compute the gun and laser gates against the final commanded aim.

findings.title: FFA latch is looser than D12 and fires in squad practice: two foreign deaths, or no death at all
findings.where: environment() lines 22-87 (F += 1.5 per foreign death, += 2 per beam, += 1 per hp drop; latch at F >= 3 with 2 victims); senses.js line 172 (hpPrev not reset when a track is listed again)
findings.evidence: D12: latch only when (16 - alive) - ourKills >= 3 before 200 s, beam clue off by default, when in doubt SQUAD. tools/review_tactics/s07_ffa_unit.js (synthetic observations): (a) alive 16 -> 14 without kill events latches at t=20.6 with F=3; (b) with no death at all, three mechs seen again after 6 s with 60 hp less (a drone or the zone hurt them out of sight; hpPrev is stale) latch at t=30. In dev-simulator squad matches the latch fired in seed 118 at t=28.1 (F=3.5) and, on the earlier house table, in seed 6 in three of four runs (s05_ffa_latch.js shows the last step: a listed house bot 94 hp lower than when last seen). After the latch the idle pull is off, the default stance is DEFENSIVE with the silent first-shot policy, and plating is picked first.
findings.fix: Implement D12 exactly: one counter, deaths not matched by our kill events inside 0.6 s, latch at 3 before t = 200 s; remove the hp-drop clue, keep the beam clue behind the preset (off). Reset hpPrev / hpPrevT whenever a track is listed after a gap. Ship practice builds with env 'squad'.

findings.title: Behaviour depends on the wall clock: the same seed gives 4 or 6 kills
findings.where: evalMaybe() lines 158-165, act() lines 350, 361 and 371-373 (slowMs -> budgetScale); mover.js lines 52 and 154 (planMinMs 12 ms of a 27.5 ms window); stance.js line 223
findings.evidence: D10 forbids clock-dependent behaviour (a bot with it scored 3.67-3.90 with identical code). tools/review_tactics/s06_determinism.js, same process, same seed 6: first run (counters skipped 1, overruns 2, slow 4) -> 4 kills, 65.7 s alive, FFA latch at 29.0 s; second and third run (skipped 0) -> 6 kills, 69.55 s, latch at 63.4 s, different trace hash. A further run of the same seed elsewhere gave 5 kills and no latch. Path planning is skipped whenever less than 12 ms remain, position evaluation below 6 ms, the hide search below 4 ms, and one decision slower than 15 ms halves the ray and A* budgets for the next 20 decisions. On the one-CPU sandbox these fuses will trip more often than here.
findings.fix: Bound every stage by operation counts only (rays, expansions, candidates) sized for the 8 ms target; remove budgetScale and the planMinMs / optMinMs tests from the normal path and keep a single emergency fuse near the real deadline that only reuses the previous action; count its trips in debugState and make the test suite fail when it trips.

findings.title: Final zone phases: stand-off legs fight the zone; 800-900 hp of zone damage before the circle closes when an enemy stands on the centre
findings.where: zoneGoal() lines 121-141, zoneCheck() 144-170, zoneLegs() 172-176; brain.js fightLegs() lines 284-288 (fallbacks without a zone test); senses.js line 360 (nrEff)
findings.evidence: tools/review_tactics/s04_zone_late.js (circles 70 -> 25 -> 0 m with the real hold / shrink times, hp frozen so only the zone is measured). Alone: fine (1 decision outside, 26 hp). With a mech that walks to the next centre and stands there (B passive, C shooting): 31-37 decisions outside before the circle has closed, 819-936 hp of zone damage, 37-43 switches between ZONE and FIGHT / DISENGAGE in 75 s, and during the final shrink 189-195 of 240 decisions more than 3 m from the final centre (D9: stand on the moving centre). The fight legs keep asking for the stand-off range (110 m) inside a 25 m circle, ZONE pulls back when the margin drops under 4 s, and so on. ZONE legs also walk in a straight line under fire.
findings.fix: From next_radius <= 70 (D9) the legs belong to the zone: goal = next centre, in the final shrink the moving centre, walk onto it and keep pushing; allow only a strafe that stays inside min(radius, next radius) - 3 m and clamp rPref to that; do not hand the legs back to FIGHT while the circle is smaller than the stand-off band. Use 0.5 of the next radius as the zone goal (D9) instead of 0.8.

findings.title: Opening and idle time: the mech stands still at a wall for 15 s per match before the first contact
findings.where: holdLegs() lines 168-196; stance.js idleLegs() lines 170-181 (needs a previously seen enemy and 20 s); economy.js chooseLoot() radii (cubes 60 m, crates 80 m, no drones)
findings.evidence: tools/review_tactics/stats2.js, 60 squad matches (seeds 101-160): before the first damage (mean 32.7 s) the brain spends 15.4 s per match in HOLD with speed < 0.5 m/s, 7.7 s of it with a crate known within 150 m, 4.5 s in LOOT and 0.1 s in the pull; stats3.js: of 584 fully quiet decisions later in the match 250 are spent standing still. The first hit then often comes from outside the 120 degree wedge (the s15 trace starts with two rear hits). D6: farm ground crates within 150 m and drones within 170 m while out of contact at hp >= 90%, stop at 210 s or at 10 cubes plus a laser.
findings.fix: Replace the stand-at-a-wall default by the D6 loop: nearest ground crate within 150 m (approach to 30 m, shoot, collect), drones within 170 m (38 m, stand and shoot), weapon pickups by rank; when nothing is known walk toward the zone centre region with the torso scanning. Let the idle pull start from sound bearings as well, not only from a seen enemy.

findings.title: Hide cells: recomputed while running, often on the attacker's side, reached in only a third of the attempts
findings.where: makeHideSearch(): run() lines 268-295 (cost, line 287 penalty 0.6 toward threat 0 only), maintain() lines 297-311 (restart from the current position when the cell stops being hidden)
findings.evidence: tools/review_tactics/stats2.js and stats3.js, 60 squad matches: 467 hide-leg episodes, 146 reach the cell (< 3 m); the cell jumps by more than 6 m 184 times during an episode and 124 of the new cells are farther away (in a match trace the distance to the cell grew 34 -> 41 m while boosting at 19.5 m/s toward it); 39% of hide decisions use boost; of 4353 exposed retreat decisions 615 (14%) move within 60 degrees of the direction to the attacker, 359 of them with the attacker inside 80 m, and 57 of 430 exposed retreat episodes end more than 10 m closer to it.
findings.fix: Require the cell to be on the far side: the first 15 m of the path must increase the distance to every mech that has a line, and the cell must be hidden from the attacker's position extrapolated 3 s along its approach. Commit to a chosen cell while heading for it (re-search only when it has been exposed for 0.5 s or a clearly better one exists), and stop boosting toward a cell that moved. With the D3 thresholds most of these retreats disappear anyway.

findings.title: Any listed mech at any range is a target and the gun opens at 120 m on average (D0 guard, D2 flight-time gate and D5 candidate rule are not implemented)
findings.where: selectTarget() candidate loop lines 86-92; firecontrol.js line 154 (range test 0.97 * 230 m only)
findings.evidence: tools/review_tactics/stats2.js, 60 squad matches: the first gun shot at a mech is fired at a mean range of 122 m; 17% of all gun shots are fired beyond 130 m and hit 46% (49% at 130-170 m, 37% beyond), against 85-92% under 100 m; two different mechs damage us within 30 s of the first hit. In one traced match the whole first magazine went to a mech at 125-160 m (5 hits) and the hunter then arrived at 55 m during the 2.4 s reload. D2: no gun fire at a bullet flight above 0.55 s unless the target was steady for 0.6 s or airborne; D5: candidates are hostile mechs, mechs inside the band + 40 m, or anything after 20 s unengaged at hp >= 90%; D0: no first shot at a non-hostile mech in the first 40 s. A crude override (gunRangeFrac 0.57) alone was neutral in the dev simulator (-0.15 +- 0.13), so the gain depends on the steadiness test and on how the real squad reacts to being shot.
findings.fix: Implement the three rules as written: hostility flag per track (damaged us in 4 s, or aims within 12 degrees with a line inside 160 m), candidate filter in selectTarget, and the flight-time gate (sol.t > 0.55 s needs |dv| < 2 m/s over the last 0.6 s or an airborne target) next to the range test. Keep long shots for kill-secures.

findings.title: Fighting range still follows the old stance table (110-115 m gun, 120 m laser) instead of D2
findings.where: rPrefGun / bandLo / bandHi / rPrefLaser (lines 29-30) and STANCES (lines 72-77); brain.js fightLegs() lines 238-247; no dead band in mover.standoff()
findings.evidence: D2: gun only hold 75 m (band 55-95), laser preset far 150 m or mid 115 m, lightning 28 m. tools/review_tactics/stats5.js, 60 squad matches: of the gun-only FIGHT decisions with a line 26% are inside 55-95 m, 39% at 95-125 m, 22% beyond 125 m. Physics from the scenario scripts, for the A/B: our hit rate against a house-like strafer is 78% at 75 m, about 60% at 100 m, 43% at 130 m (s12_revlead.js); an exact first-order gun hits our jink 72% at 75 m, 45% at 100 m, 30% at 130 m (s10_jink.js). The override rPrefGun 75 / band 55-95 alone was neutral in the dev simulator (-0.06 +- 0.10); D2 rests on real scores, so this has to be decided on the real scorer.
findings.fix: Add the D2 numbers as named presets (gunRange 75 / 55-95 with full stick in and 0.7 out, laserRange far 150 / mid 115 with the back-off and boost-away rules, lightning 28 m) and a real dead band in standoff(); make one of them the default per the lead's decision and submit exactly one preset change at a time.

findings.title: Bullet-aware dodge and magazine-rhythm use (D4) are absent; the jink alone leaves 72% hits at 75 m
findings.where: senseShells() lines 311-328 (gun bullets are only counted into B.bulletsSeen, which nothing reads); mover.js standoff() jink lines 93-97
findings.evidence: D4 calls the bullet-aware dodge the main defence [T] and asks for per-shooter bullet counts (12 shots then 2.5 s silence) and an extra reversal at magazine start. None of it exists (also listed as missing in notes/brain_checkpoint.md). tools/review_tactics/s10_jink.js, exact first-order gun at R, 4 seeds x 60 s: the shipped reversal interval U(0.5,1.0) is hit 72% / 45% / 30% at 75 / 100 / 130 m; no reversal 99 / 95 / 90%. Caution for the D4 strafe preset: U(0.8,1.6) is hit 80 / 65 / 52% in the same scenario and U(0.35,0.7) 64 / 38 / 24%, so the slower interval should not be adopted without the bullet dodge and an A/B.
findings.fix: Track enemy gun projectiles (id, pos, vel), compute the closest approach to our predicted position over 0.9 s, and when it is under radius + 1.2 m blend a perpendicular sidestep (walkable and inside the zone, else brake / reverse) with weight 0.9 into the leg command; count bullets per shooter to time approaches and crossings into its 2.5 s reload; add one reversal when a magazine starts.

findings.title: A laser charge that is already running is kept during the shell dodge and outside the zone (half speed for up to 0.5 s)
findings.where: run(), laser branch lines 175-189 (B.noCharge is only tested on line 190, where a charge starts, and on line 132)
findings.evidence: Spec section 2: never charge when ZONE or DODGE needs full speed. tools/review_tactics/s13_charge_zone.js (synthetic observations): with the charge at 0.3 s when a mortar shell is predicted on us, or when in_zone turns false, the brain keeps the laser trigger down for five more decisions (0.3 -> 0.8) while the legs boost in the dodge / ZONE leg. Charging halves the speed (also the boost speed in the simulator), so about 5 m of the escape is lost against a 7 m splash radius.
findings.fix: When B.noCharge is set and a charge is running, release at once (the beam fires at min_frac or better; aim it at the target if the gate allows) instead of holding to full; equivalently set laserKeep = false unless full is reached within one decision.

findings.title: Supply drop: walks in at once and waits in the ring for up to 25 s
findings.where: chooseDrop() lines 88-111 (only an upper bound on the path, contest test at selection time only), dropLegs() lines 144-148
findings.evidence: D6: arrive no more than 3 s before the landing, only within 250 m, never contested (leave when a mech is within 60 m of the ring), not beyond 70 m once landed, no waiting in the ring. tools/review_tactics/s21_offer_drop.js (synthetic): a drop 30 m away that lands in 20 s puts the brain in DROP mode immediately, i.e. about 17 s standing in a ring every mech can see on its map (10 s -> 7 s). There is no 250 m / 70 m limit and no leave rule once inside; DROP is 0.6% of the decisions in squad matches, so the cost today is small.
findings.fix: Start walking when pathTime >= lands_in - 3 s (hold or loot nearby until then), add the 250 m and 70 m limits, and re-check the contest rule every decision: leave the ring when a tracked mech is within 60 m of it.

findings.title: Upgrade order is the old section 5 list, not D7
findings.where: pick() lines 167-189 with UPGRADE_ORDER in params.js lines 79-80
findings.evidence: D7: plating > armor > nanites > laser_damage > laser_charge (laser held) > lightning_efficiency (lightning held) > gun_damage > gun_rate > lightning_range > lightning_chain > gyros > servos > gun_mag > ... The code takes nanites on the first two offers, then gun_damage, laser_damage, plating, armor; lightning_efficiency, lightning_chain, jets and gun_velocity are not in the list (score 100). tools/review_tactics/s21_offer_drop.js: 8 of 8 sample offers are answered differently from D7 (for example [plating, nanites, gun_damage] -> nanites; [lightning_efficiency, servos, gyros] while holding lightning -> servos). D7 carries grade [T, no A/B], so the size of the effect is unknown.
findings.fix: Replace UPGRADE_ORDER by the D7 list with its two held-weapon conditions and delete the nanites-first special case; keep the order in PARAMS so a preset can swap it.

findings.title: Section 4 / 6 rules that exist only as parameters: peek / hide cycle, re-hit of a winning duel, relocation cells, first-shot policy
findings.where: peekMax / hideMin / firstShot in STANCES, rehitS, relocateMin, evalRays, anchorMaxDist, anchorPull, coverShare, lootAimRange, npcDpsIn (never read); B.jinkTurn in brain.js line 134 / mover.js line 230 (never set)
findings.evidence: A grep of every PARAMS / STANCES key against the brain modules finds these names only where they are defined or copied. So: no peek / hide cycle with exposure limits (section 4; only reloadhide within 8 m and beamhide exist), no "hit a winning target at least every 4 s" rule (HEAL at hp < 90% once the target has been out of sight for 6 s lets a 300 hp enemy regenerate fully), no relocation to another peek cell >= 10 m away (M3 became the no-jink run of finding 4), the position evaluation has no ray budget parameter. In SQUAD the missing peek cycle costs little because D3 forbids hiding when not LOSING; the missing re-hit rule matters when a damaged hunter breaks the line.
findings.fix: Either delete the dead parameters or implement the two that matter for kills: (1) while the target has lost more hp than we have, do not enter HEAL; re-acquire it within rehitS (walk to the nearest cell with a line, chase below 50% hp for 6 s); (2) keep the peek cycle for the FFA posture only.

findings.title: Energy rule for lightning is dead code and the boost reserve is below the lightning reserve
findings.where: legs() line 316 (condition ends with && !B.me.gun); retreatLegs() line 211 and PARAMS.boostReserve 25 against lightReserve 35
findings.evidence: Spec section 2: never spend energy on boost when lightning is the short-range answer and an enemy is inside 60 m. The guard only applies when no gun is held, which never happens in SQUAD (the gun is always kept). The retreat boost runs down to 25 energy on every tick with a hide cell within 40 m, while lightning refuses to fire below 35 (15 for a kill-secure): after a retreat boost the lightning is silent until the tank refills at 18 per s. Read from the code; in the traces the rush with lightning arrives with about 60 energy, i.e. about 2 s of arcs above the reserve.
findings.fix: Drop the !B.me.gun term (apply the guard whenever lightning is held and a mech is inside 60 m), and use max(boostReserve, lightReserve + 10) as the boost floor while lightning is held.

summary:
Adversarial review of the brain's behaviour against BRAIN_SPEC_V2.md (Doctrine V4 block D0-D12, then sections 2-8). No file under bot/ was edited, and bot/lib was unchanged during the review (brain.js 05:51:33, stance / tactics / params 05:52:27). All scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-yang-mills-workbench/c2b3cfae-3f5d-5b6f-8fe6-a6e757d1bb60/scratchpad/mechbot/tools/review_tactics/ (scen.js and lib_trace.js are the harnesses; s01-s23 are scenarios; stats*.js and ab.js run squad matches in sim/). The conformance check and tools/test_brain.js were not re-run.

**Main result.** 23 findings, most damaging first. The two with the clearest effect are parameter-sized:

1. The gun trigger waits for a cooldown read-out <= 0.05 s, so the gun fires every 0.30 s instead of 0.24 s (64 against 72 shots per 30 s).
2. LAST-STAND is entered at 65-70% hp, even in a 1 v 1, and its bastion legs stand still.

In 24 duels at 75 m against a standing exact-lead gun the shipped brain kills 13 (11 when the enemy starts behind us). With the bastion disabled and readyCd 0.10 it kills 24 (22).

**Most of Doctrine V4 is not in the code yet.** The engagement, healing, economy, range, candidate, dodge, latch and upgrade rules still follow the older sections 4-7. Measured in 60 squad matches of the dev simulator:
- 353 fight break-offs at a mean hp of 82%, of which 12 are LOSING by D3.
- 59% of HEAL decisions happen at hp >= 55%.
- 71% of kills leave their cubes on the ground.
- 34 matches end gun-only, although a laser or lightning pickup lay within 60 m in 45.

**Other confirmed bugs:**
- The jink is off during every reload against laser or mortar holders (+40% damage taken).
- A drone hijacks the target in a duel (8/8 kills become 1/8).
- Partial paths make the mover flip-flop (squad seed 156: 42 s in place, then 1460 hp of zone damage).
- The torso veto can leave the torso pointing at neither enemy.
- The FFA latch fires on two foreign deaths, or on none.
- The same seed gives 4 or 6 kills depending on the wall clock.
- With an enemy on the final zone centre, 800-900 hp go to the zone before the circle closes.

**Dev-simulator A/B, parameter overrides only.** The simulator's house table changed during the review, so absolute scores are not comparable across runs; the first run (old table, 100 seeds) showed nothing outside its noise.

| Override (seeds 101+) | Result |
| --- | --- |
| shipped | 2.80-2.87 |
| readyCd 0.10 | +0.23 +- 0.15 |
| bastion off | +0.12 +- 0.08 |
| both | 3.13-3.16 |
| both, plus fight-on and heal thresholds near D3 | 3.30 +- 0.19 |
| healExit 0.7 alone | +0.12 +- 0.09 |

Each single difference is within about 1.5 standard errors; the ranking of the findings rests on the scenario scripts and the doctrine's own evidence.

**Checked and found sound:**
- Yaw from +x counter-clockwise, wrap at +-pi, pitch sign, rear-arc test, muzzle offset, and target height with cubes.
- Latency is applied once. It is 0.05 s too long for a ready gun, worth about 1-2 points of hit rate at 110 m; the correction is part of finding 1.
- The fire gate is not too strict: at 150 and 190 m the lost trigger time came from blocked muzzle lines on the map, not from the gate. There is no shot at 200 m because vision ends there.
- Laser fire control: 2.40 s cycle, 92-100% beam hits at 100-190 m.
- The lead-halving rule for reversing targets is neutral against house-like reversal intervals.
- Normal zone phases, apart from the path bug.

**Not exercised:** closed-loop mortar fire, real mortar shells in flight, and supply-drop capture.
